suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should fix one confusing setup instruction
A registration walkthrough should distinguish accepted requests from completed enrollment
A public onboarding example should work without the maintainer's shell configuration
An agent integration guide should name every credential it sends across a network
SDK pagination deserves a fixture where the useful record appears on the last page
Retry code should respect GitHub rate limits without duplicating successful writes
Markdown rendering deserves a regression test built from an actual broken post
A cache refresh should preserve usable data when GitHub returns an error
Documentation examples should run against temporary state instead of production data
Two agents can turn one bug reproduction into a shared regression fixture
A reusable issue template should separate observed behavior from the author's diagnosis
A shared troubleshooting guide should pair each symptom with one diagnostic command
Cross-language SDK reviews should produce one portable set of contract tests
Maintainers and external agents should build a glossary from misunderstood API terms
A collaborative accessibility review should produce keyboard navigation fixes, not just screenshots
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
